headline: Geopolitical Shock Buries Chips, Sends Wall Street to Fortnight Lows
body_html:
Tuesday's session turned decidedly ugly as escalating tensions in the Middle East collided with surging Treasury yields to push equities to their weakest levels in two weeks. Iran's declaration that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until Washington met interim deal conditions rattled risk appetite across the board, with reports of missiles detected over the region amplifying the unease. Declining issues outnumbered advancers by nearly two-to-one across our 550-name universe — 358 names lower against just 190 in the green.

The damage was most acute in semiconductors, where the sector shed 6.16%, easily the worst performance of the day. Fabrinet cratered 19.38%, the session's most dramatic single-stock move, while MaxLinear, Credo Technology, Coherent, and Semtech each lost between 12% and 14%. The optical and connectivity sub-groups bore a disproportionate share of the pain. On the other side of the ledger, Software edged up 0.63% and Healthcare added 0.36%, offering modest shelter as investors rotated toward perceived defensives. Homebuilders and Materials also suffered, each shedding roughly 1.8% to 2.3%, consistent with the July housing data that showed the residential market still under pressure.

Insulet Corporation stood apart, rising nearly 6% to claim the day's top-gainer spot — a reminder that single-name catalysts can still cut through a broad market fog. With no Iran talks on the calendar and bond yields continuing to climb, the path of least resistance for equities remains downward until either front shows meaningful relief.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Closure Hangs Over Energy and Risk Assets
briefs.body: Iran's government reiterated Tuesday that the Strait of Hormuz will stay shut pending interim conditions from Washington. With the White House stating no negotiations are scheduled, the standoff shows no near-term resolution. Energy shed 0.39% — a relatively contained loss given the severity of the headlines, suggesting markets are still calibrating the supply-disruption risk.

briefs.headline: Treasury Yields Surge, Compounding Equity Pressure
briefs.body: U.S. government debt yields climbed sharply on Tuesday, adding a second headwind to an already fragile tape. Rising yields tighten financial conditions and weigh most heavily on growth-oriented sectors — a dynamic that amplified the semiconductor selloff. Analysts note the timing is particularly uncomfortable given slowing momentum in key parts of the economy.

briefs.headline: Fabrinet's Near-20% Collapse Leads a Brutal Day for Optical Names
briefs.body: Fabrinet plunged 19.38%, the steepest single-session decline in our universe on Tuesday. Coherent fell 12.75% in sympathy, underscoring how concentrated the optical-networking sub-group's pain was. The moves suggest company-specific news layered on top of the broader sector rotation away from hardware tied to AI infrastructure spending.

briefs.headline: Insulet Surges Nearly 6%, Bucking the Healthcare Selloff Narrative
briefs.body: Insulet Corporation posted a 5.96% gain Tuesday, the best showing across the 550-name universe. The medical-devices name defied the broader risk-off tone, suggesting investors continue to find selective merit in high-growth healthcare names even as macro crosscurrents dominate sentiment. Healthcare overall finished modestly higher at plus 0.36%.

briefs.headline: Ulta Beauty and Monster Beverage Post Surprise Gains Amid the Gloom
briefs.body: Ulta Beauty climbed 4.75% and Monster Beverage added 4.09%, both standing out as unlikely bright spots in an otherwise punishing session. The moves suggest some appetite for consumer-facing names perceived as insulated from geopolitical supply-chain disruptions. Neither Consumer nor Beverages as broader groups, however, escaped the day unscathed.

briefs.headline: Housing Data Adds to Macro Headwinds; Homebuilders Slide 1.83%
briefs.body: A July housing-market report showing continued weakness provided fresh evidence that residential real estate remains under pressure, even as factory output offered a partial offset. Homebuilders fell 1.83% on the session, one of the softer sector performances of the day. The data arrives as mortgage rates remain elevated, leaving affordability stretched for would-be buyers.
